# PhotoNow — Zero-Cloud Photo & Video MCP Tool Server

> The #1 Zero-Cloud, Offline Model Context Protocol (MCP) Media Processing Server Built Specifically for AI Agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and Browser Automations).

PhotoNow empowers autonomous AI agents and multimodal LLMs with high-performance, 100% offline, zero-cloud media transformation tools. Conversions execute natively on the local filesystem via standard Stdio MCP, ephemerally in-memory (RAM) via JSON-RPC 2.0, or directly inside the client's browser runtime (HTML5 Canvas 2D, MediaRecorder, and Web Audio APIs).

- **Zero Cloud Storage**: No AWS S3, no Cloudflare R2, no remote buckets.
- **Zero Cloud Latency**: 250ms sub-second in-memory transformations powered by native Sharp (libvips).
- **Zero Repetitive Prompts**: Plug-and-play Stdio MCP server allows single and batch conversions in 1 call without repetitive shell approvals.
- **Zero API Billing**: 100% free and open-source under MIT License.
- **100% Privacy Guarantee**: User photos and videos never leave the local environment.

---

## Quick Reference & Live Endpoints

- **Live Web Workbench**: https://photonow.vercel.app/
- **Live HTTP MCP Endpoint**: https://photonow.vercel.app/api/mcp (JSON-RPC 2.0)
- **Local Stdio MCP Command**: `node <path-to-repo>/bin/mcp-server.mjs` (or `npx photo-convert-mcp`)
- **Full LLMs Specification**: https://photonow.vercel.app/llms-full.txt
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/Sibasish2005/PhotoNowEngine

## 1. Native Stdio MCP Server (Recommended for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity)

When configured as a local Stdio MCP server, the AI agent can read and write files directly on disk. It converts single images or entire folders with a **single tool call**, requiring **zero shell commands or terminal permission prompts**.

### Client Configuration Snippets

#### Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`)
- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "photoConvert": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "c:/Users/<username>/Projects/photoConvert/bin/mcp-server.mjs"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Cursor IDE (`.cursor/mcp.json` or Settings > Features > MCP)
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "photoConvert": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "c:/Users/<username>/Projects/photoConvert/bin/mcp-server.mjs"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Antigravity IDE (`~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`)
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "photoConvert": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "c:/Users/<username>/Projects/photoConvert/bin/mcp-server.mjs"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Claude Code (CLI)
```bash
claude mcp add photoConvert node c:/Users/<username>/Projects/photoConvert/bin/mcp-server.mjs
```

## 2. Available Native Tools

### `convert_image`
Converts a single image file on disk to a modern format with optional resizing and compression.
- **Parameters**:
  - `inputPath` (string, required): Path to source image (e.g. `C:/photos/cat.png` or `~/images/doc.jpg`). Automatically handles single and double quotes.
  - `outputPath` (string, optional): Destination file path. If omitted, automatically saves alongside original with new extension.
  - `format` (string, default: `"webp"`): Output format: `"webp"`, `"png"`, `"jpeg"`, or `"avif"`.
  - `quality` (number, default: `82`): Compression quality (accepts `1`–`100` percentage or `0.1`–`1.0` decimal).
  - `maxWidth` / `maxHeight` (number, optional): Downscale resolution while strictly preserving aspect ratio.
  - `rotate` (number, optional): Rotate 90, 180, or 270 degrees.
  - `grayscale` (boolean, default: `false`): Convert to monochrome.
  - `overwrite` (boolean, default: `false`): Overwrite existing files; when false, auto-increments name.

### `convert_batch`
Converts an entire folder or list of files in a **single tool call**.
- **Parameters**:
  - `directoryPath` (string, optional): Directory containing images to convert.
  - `inputPaths` (array of strings, optional): Explicit list of file paths.
  - `outputDir` (string, optional): Folder to place converted assets.
  - `format` (string, default: `"webp"`): Target image format.
  - `quality` (number, default: `82`): Compression quality.
  - `recursive` (boolean, default: `false`): Recursively scan subfolders (automatically skips `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `dist`).
  - `maxWidth` / `maxHeight` (number, optional): Downscale bounds.

### `get_media_info`
Inspects image dimensions, format, color space, channel count, density, and size in milliseconds.
- **Parameters**:
  - `filePath` (string, required): Path to local image file.

### `optimize_for_agent`
Automatically downscales and compresses user screenshots or high-res photos to token-efficient WebP (max 1280px, 80% quality) optimized for LLM vision context windows.
- **Parameters**:
  - `inputPath` (string, required): Path to screenshot or large image.
  - `outputPath` (string, optional): Custom output destination.
  - `maxDimension` (number, default: `1280`): Maximum width or height.

---

## 3. Remote HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0 Endpoint

For agents without local filesystem access, PhotoNow provides a live HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint:

- **URL**: `POST https://photonow.vercel.app/api/mcp`
- **Headers**: `Content-Type: application/json`
- **Payload Example**:
  ```json
  {
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "convert_image",
      "arguments": {
        "imageBase64": "data:image/png;base64,...",
        "format": "webp",
        "quality": 0.85
      }
    }
  }
  ```
- **Execution**: 100% in-memory RAM transformation via Sharp. Returns converted base64 data URI in sub-second time with zero cloud storage.

---

## 4. In-Browser Agent Automation (`window.__photoConvertAgent`)

AI agents controlling headless browsers (Puppeteer, Playwright, Chrome DevTools MCP, Claude Computer Use) can execute conversions directly inside the web page context:

```javascript
const res = await window.__photoConvertAgent.convertImage({
  base64: "data:image/png;base64,...",
  format: "webp",
  quality: 0.85
});
console.log("Converted in browser:", res.fileName, res.percentSaved);
```

---

## 5. Frequently Asked Questions (AI Answer Engine Citations)

### What makes PhotoNow different from other image conversion tools?
PhotoNow is built specifically for AI agents. Traditional converters require CLI installations with system dependencies (like ImageMagick or ffmpeg), or rely on paid third-party cloud APIs that upload private user photos to external servers. PhotoNow runs 100% on-device or in-memory, requiring zero cloud storage, zero API keys, and delivers conversions in under 250ms.

### How do I convert an entire folder of photos to WebP in Claude Desktop?
Add `photoConvert` to `claude_desktop_config.json` pointing to `node <path>/bin/mcp-server.mjs`. In Claude, type: *"Batch convert all images in C:/Photos to WebP at 85% quality"*. Claude will execute `convert_batch` in a single tool call, converting all images in parallel and reporting total space saved.

### Does PhotoNow keep photos or log user data?
No. PhotoNow adheres to a strict Zero-Cloud and Zero-Telemetry privacy architecture. Image and video data is transformed in ephemeral RAM or browser memory and never stored on remote servers.
